title: Asia stocks rebound as SpaceX, Super Micro results lift chipmakers
full_text:
Wall Street ends higher on surge in health care stocks, solid earnings
Investing.com -- Asian stocks advanced on Wednesday as stronger-than-expected earnings from major beneficiaries of the artificial intelligence boom revived confidence in the technology trade, helping regional chipmakers rebound after last week’s selloff.
Brent traded above $110 a barrel as attacks near the Strait of Hormuz threatened supplies and U.S. data pointed to another crude-stock draw, fuelling inflation concerns even as strong earnings offered some relief to tech investors.
Wall Street was mixed overnight, with the Dow Jones Industrial Average rising 1% and the S&P 500 gaining 0.3%, while the Nasdaq Composite ended little changed; in Asian trade, Nasdaq 100 futures climbed 1% and S&P 500 futures advanced 0.4%.
SpaceX shares jumped 8.1% in extended trading after the company reported better-than-expected earnings, while Super Micro Computer surged 16% after its preliminary results exceeded forecasts. Netflix shares fell nearly 6% in after-hours trade as a weaker-than-expected fourth-quarter outlook overshadowed its third-quarter earnings beat.
South Korea, Taiwan lead chipmaker rebound
The MSCI Asia Pacific index climbed 1.1%, snapping two sessions of losses. South Korea’s KOSPI jumped 3.7%, while Taiwan’s Taiex gained around 1.4%, as semiconductor stocks led the recovery. Japan’s Nikkei 225 and the TOPIX advanced over 1%.
South Korean memory-chip makers led gains, with Samsung Electronics rising 7.1% and SK Hynix climbing 6.2%. Japan’s Kioxia advanced 3.2% and Murata Manufacturing added 3.4%. Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co. rose 0.8% and Largan Precision gained 3.8%.
The rebound followed fresh evidence of strong demand for AI computing infrastructure. Super Micro said it expected quarterly revenue of $18.5 billion to $19.5 billion, well above its previous guidance of $14.5 billion to $15.5 billion and analysts’ expectations.
SpaceX reported quarterly revenue of $14.6 billion, up 161% year-on-year, and profit of $4.4 billion, supported by rapid growth in its AI business.
Its results helped restore some confidence in AI-linked companies after concerns about valuations, financing requirements and the returns on heavy infrastructure spending unsettled markets last week.
AI infrastructure stocks nevertheless saw sharply divergent moves. South Korean data-centre company Elice Group surged around 30% in Seoul, rebounding after one of the country’s weakest IPO debuts on record. Its shares had opened 16% below their offering price and subsequently plunged as much as 33% on Tuesday.
Australia’s NextDC, however, sank around 40% after cutting its financial outlook as delays to electricity-network upgrades at its Melbourne M3 data centre postponed contracted capacity and revenue.
Regional stocks mixed as Japan trade misses forecasts and CATL slumps
Japan’s September trade data were weaker than expected, with exports and imports both missing forecasts and the trade deficit widening more than anticipated.
Elsewhere, Hong Kong’s Hang Seng fell 0.2%, mainland China’s CSI 300 slipped 0.7% and the Shanghai Composite lost 0.4%. Australia’s S&P/ASX 200 eased 0.1%, while New Zealand’s NZX 50 rose 0.7% and Singapore’s Straits Times Index gained 0.8%.
Indonesia’s Jakarta Composite fell 1.12%, while India’s Nifty 50 futures declined 1.1%.
China’s Contemporary Amperex Technology (CATL) shares slumped 8% to a 15-month low after the world’s largest EV battery maker reported weaker-than-expected third-quarter earnings, with profit growth slowing to its weakest pace in nearly two years amid cooling Chinese auto sales and intensifying competition.
Attention now turns to a busy earnings slate for evidence that companies can justify the substantial capital being poured into computing infrastructure.
Meta Platforms and Tesla are due to report later on Wednesday, with investors watching closely for updates on AI investment and consumer demand.

title: Trump, in North Carolina, says Republicans will defy midterm odds
full_text:
By Jacob Bogage
GREENVILLE, North Carolina, Oct 20 (Reuters) - With his approval rating at record lows, President Donald Trump attempted to defy political gravity in a pep rally in North Carolina on Tuesday, urging voters to support his favored Senate candidate in a race some Republican groups have already given up on.
Trump has embarked on a campaign blitz ahead of the November 3 midterm elections, traveling more than 29,000 miles (46,671 km) since late September to boost Republican candidates — and his second stop in North Carolina in as many months was a signal of how much is at stake in this southern state.
Polls show former Democratic Governor Roy Cooper with a commanding lead over Republican Michael Whatley, a former senior party official, in a Senate race that could help decide the balance of power in Washington.
The two are running to fill the seat of retiring Republican Thom Tillis, a one-time Trump ally, who split with the president over his landmark tax bill and defense policy.
Tillis told Politico in a Tuesday interview that his fellow Republicans were headed toward “a train wreck” and a "whoop ass" in November.
But Trump, speaking in the eastern city of Greenville on Tuesday night, predicted Whatley would prove the doubters wrong.
"I think you’re gonna see some amazing results," he told hundreds of supporters who gathered on the grounds of the local airport. "They never poll us right. We have more spirit."
’WE NEED YOU’
Trump won North Carolina in each of his three presidential runs, but Democrats are banking on a breakthrough performance this year, with polls showing a clear majority of Americans dissatisfied with rising prices and the war in Iran.
The president’s approval rating has fallen to 31%, according to the latest Reuters/Ipsos survey, the lowest mark at any point during his two terms in office.
In early voting in North Carolina, Democrats have cast more ballots than Republicans by a two-to-one margin, according to state data.
Republican candidates on Tuesday night implored voters to turn out early.
"This is a Republican majority district," said Laurie Buckhout, a Trump-backed candidate running for a congressional seat in a mostly rural eastern district. “We have the momentum. We have the message. Now we need you."
Republicans hold 10 of the state’s 14 House seats, but a handful of districts are viewed as battlegrounds this cycle — and have attracted significant spending.
Buckhout’s race against Democratic Representative Don Davis has drawn $21 million in outside money since September 1, making it the third most expensive contest in the country, according to a Reuters analysis of campaign filings.
In the state’s mountainous west, outside groups have spent $14.5 million on the race between Democrat Jamie Ager and Republican Jennifer Balkcom.
Whatley, by contrast, has largely been abandoned by the national party apparatus. The Senate Leadership Fund, the primary PAC supporting Republican candidates for the upper chamber, cut off spending in North Carolina earlier this month as Cooper posted double-digit leads in poll after poll.
’TIGHTEN THAT SHIP UP’
Trump’s popularity has cratered since he ordered military strikes on Iran in February alongside US ally Israel, triggering a surge in gasoline and diesel prices.
Some 68% of Americans disapprove of Trump’s handling of the economy, Reuters/Ipsos has found, including 37% of self-identified Republicans.
Taylor Smith, who described herself as a housewife in Greenville, told Reuters she had only ever voted Republican, but the drama of the Trump administration had her thinking twice.
Disorganization within the White House was bleeding into policy, she said, revealing Trump’s lack of focus.
“Anything good that could be happening is being co-opted by the tomfoolery that’s just going on,” Smith said.
"I hate these gas prices," she added, urging the president to “tighten that ship up.”
As he has in events across the country, Trump heralded what he said were new local investments on Tuesday night.
Sibelco, an industrial minerals mining and processing company, was expanding its operations in North Carolina, Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick announced on stage without providing specifics.
Sibelco did not immediately respond to a request for comment.
Trump said the US Defense Department would also invest $1.5 billion in semiconductor chip production in North Carolina, but did not say where or how the money would be spent.
Toward the end of his speech, the president repeated his promise to give $5,000 to every US adult should Republicans maintain their hold on Congress.
"If we lose," he said, "you get nothing."

title: Asian chip stocks rally as Super Micro forecast revives AI demand optimism
full_text:
Investing.com -- Asian chipmakers and artificial intelligence-related stocks rallied on Wednesday after stronger-than-expected preliminary revenue guidance from Super Micro Computer offered relief to investors concerned about the sustainability of spending on AI infrastructure.
South Korea’s KOSPI jumped 4.6% to 5,805.63, while Japan’s Nikkei 225 rose 1.7% to 65,162. South Korea’s Samsung Electronics climbed 6.2% and SK Hynix gained 6.5%, while Japan’s Kioxia Holdings rose 4%, TDK advanced 3.5% and Murata Manufacturing added 3.7%.
Super Micro said it expects revenue for the first quarter of fiscal 2027, ended September 30, to range between $18.5 billion and $19.5 billion, well above its previous forecast of $14.5 billion to $15.5 billion and analyst expectations of around $15 billion.
The company also raised its preliminary gross margin outlook to 12%–12.5%, from 10.4%–10.8%, citing a more favourable customer and product mix.
The AI server maker’s shares rose about 12% in after-hours trading on Tuesday following the update. The figures are preliminary and unaudited, with the company scheduled to report its full results on November 3.
The guidance provided a fresh sign that demand for computing systems used to train and run AI models remains strong. Super Micro assembles servers incorporating processors and accelerators from suppliers including Nvidia and AMD, making its sales a useful indicator of demand for data-centre hardware.
The rebound follows a sharp sell-off in technology stocks last week, when rising bond yields and questions over the cost of financing AI infrastructure prompted investors to reassess valuations and the returns companies may earn from heavy spending. Concerns over debt-funded data-centre expansion, including those surrounding cloud computing provider CoreWeave, have added to market volatility.
Elsewhere in the region, Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co. rose 0.8%, while Hong Kong-listed Z.AI gained 4.7%. In mainland China, Foxconn Industrial Internet advanced 3.1% and Luxshare Precision rose 2.5%, reflecting strength in parts of the AI hardware supply chain.
Investors will look to upcoming technology earnings for further evidence that demand is translating into sustainable revenue and profitability, rather than simply driving another burst of enthusiasm for AI-related stocks.

title: NextDC shares plunge 42% to a near nine-year low after outlook cut
full_text:
Wall Street ends higher on surge in health care stocks, solid earnings
Investing.com -- Nextdc (ASX:NXT) shares plunged to a near nine-year low on Wednesday after the Australian data centre operator sharply cut its fiscal 2027 earnings outlook, citing delays to power infrastructure at its M3 Melbourne facility that will defer the delivery and billing of contracted capacity.
Shares fell 42.1% to A$5.32, their lowest level since January 17, 2018, while the broader S&P/ASX 200 was little changed.
NextDC now expects FY27 net revenue of A$475 million to A$500 million, down from its previous forecast of A$615 million to A$640 million. Underlying earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortisation are forecast at A$245 million to A$265 million, compared with the earlier range of A$385 million to A$410 million.
The revisions follow delays to electricity network works by Jemena Electricity Networks, which has suspended parts of the project because of community and stakeholder opposition. The next increase in grid supply to M3 is now expected in FY28, pushing back the delivery and billing of contracted capacity.
NextDC said the revised FY27 guidance excludes revenue and underlying EBITDA from affected M3 customer contracts, including capacity already billing, because the existing grid supply cannot be relied upon to support the full contracted power ramp.
The affected contracts remain in place, but the company is assessing potential service-level credits, termination rights and whether contractual relief may be available.
The company also cut FY27 capital expenditure guidance to A$4.5 billion to A$5 billion from A$5.25 billion to A$5.75 billion.
It has put new development projects and land acquisitions on hold while reviewing spending priorities, with the board expected to announce the outcome by its annual general meeting on November 20.
Planning decisions for later stages of the Melbourne project are also delayed until 2027, as Victoria enters a caretaker period ahead of its November 28 state election.

title: OpenAI says its AI agents weakened internal monitoring system
full_text:
Wall Street ends higher on surge in health care stocks, solid earnings
By Carlos Méndez
Oct 20 (Reuters) - OpenAI said on Tuesday that two of its AI agents weakened parts of an internal monitoring system designed to detect misbehavior, the latest case of AI agents acting in ways their developers did not intend them to.
While the ChatGPT maker said the incidents happened during internal coding tasks and were not deemed its most severe, the disclosure highlights even the systems developers rely on to catch AI misbehavior are vulnerable to the agents they monitor.
The disclosure also comes amid growing concerns that AI safety efforts are lagging behind the rapid development of increasingly powerful systems. Researchers have warned that advanced AI agents could become harder to monitor and control as they gain greater autonomy.
Developers, including IPO-bound rivals OpenAI and Anthropic, have revealed in recent months instances of their AI agents accessing external systems without authorization.
OpenAI said On Tuesday a GPT-6.1 Sol agent working on an internal testing task on October 3 suppressed automatic security alerts after deciding an earlier instruction not to send Slack messages also covered safety notifications.
In a separate incident on October 6, a GPT-6 Astra agent removed a safety monitor while copying an existing piece of code and later incorrectly claimed it had not done so, OpenAI said.
"In both cases, the agents considered whether monitoring safeguards should be preserved, but interpreted routine coding instructions as permission to weaken them," the company said.
OpenAI said it was making it harder for models to disable monitoring, adding that it does not "yet have a satisfying explanation for this behavior".
The San Francisco-based company said it was testing whether its models might have a tendency to avoid being monitored and look for reasons to justify doing so.

title: Musk on possible SpaceX-Tesla merger; Meta to report - what’s moving markets
full_text:
Investing.com - Futures connected to the S&P and Nasdaq edge up, as investors assess a raft of corporate earnings, as well as ongoing uncertainty around the artificial intelligence trade and the Middle East conflict. Elon Musk says committees have been formed to explore a possible blockbuster merger of SpaceX and Tesla. AI player Anthropic reportedly posts a surge in first-half revenue, but flags a range of risks ahead of its potential initial public offering. Meta Platforms is due to unveil earnings after the closing bell.
1. Futures broadly higher
U.S. stock futures pointed mostly higher on Wednesday. By 03:01 ET (07:01 GMT), the S&P 500 futures contract had risen by 13 points, or 0.2%, Nasdaq 100 futures had climbed by 148 points, or 0.5%, and Dow futures were broadly unchanged.
The main averages on Wall Street finished in mixed fashion on Tuesday, with the benchmark S&P 500 and blue-chip both notching gains, while the tech-heavy Nasdaq ended a touch lower.
Early in the session, unconfirmed reports that Qatar and Pakistan had put forward a proposal to revive talks to conclude the Iran war briefly sent oil prices down to $106 a barrel from $112 a barrels. The rumors bolstered equity-market sentiment, which has been dented in recent sessions by worries over the sustainability of debt-fueled AI infrastructure spending and elevated borrowing costs.
"The relief from energy that played out late in the European session meant equities rallied as investors overcame some of their earlier AI jitters," analysts at Deutsche Bank said in a note.
Yet benchmark Brent crude futures later moved higher, with traders reacting to a report that Iran’s president believes "the U.S. will attack again if we negotiate." Brent was last floating around $110 a barrel.
Meanwhile, tech-heavy indices were relative underperformers. A tracker of semiconductor stocks, in particular, inched down by 0.29%, although the index did pare back much of its initial losses. Neocloud CoreWeave, which has become a figurehead of the AI fears, also bounced.
2. Committees formed to explore SpaceX-Tesla merger - Musk
SpaceX and Tesla have formed committees to explore a potential merger, according to Elon Musk, lifting shares of both firms in extended hours trading.
Speaking in a call with investors after SpaceX unveiled its second quarterly earnings since a blockbuster initial public offering earlier this year, Musk said the committees have not reached an agreement on "the terms of any transaction."
Musk, who serves as CEO of both companies and is not on either committee, added that there is "no guarantee" a deal will eventually be reached, but stressed that he does believe there is "a lot of merit" to a tie-up.
Bringing together SpaceX and Tesla would see the world’s largest commercial rocket launcher and satellite operator join forces with the second-biggest electric car manufacturer.
In the third quarter, SpaceX notched revenue of $14.6 billion, a more than 160% surge from a year ago and above analysts’ estimates. Profit stood at $4.4 billion, while capital expenditures climbed to $19.6 billion. Tesla is slated to report after the closing bell later today.
3. Anthropic S-1 shows sharp revenue growth, looming risks - reports
Anthropic is raking in huge sales, yet faces a range of possible risks ahead of a much-anticipated IPO that could value the Claude-creator at $2 trillion, media reports said.
Citing new disclosures, the reports highlighted that it is unclear where Anthropic will obtain the massive computing capacity needed to underpin its popular AI models.
At the same time, the San Francisco-based group flagged that a "significant portion" of its revenue will come from only a "limited" number of customers for the foreseeable future. In the first six months of the year, Anthropic generated $16.3 billion -- and one-fifth of that derived from just two clients.
The company recorded a net loss of over $80 billion, up from a loss of $13 billion a year earlier, largely because of an accounting adjustment.
Anthropic, whose CEO Dario Amodei has publicly warned about the dangers posed by rapidly advancing AI, also noted uncertainty around how it would protect itself from liabilities linked to the technology.

title: Starlink access in Ukraine a decision for Musk, not White House, Rubio says
full_text:
By Gram Slattery
MUMBAI, Oct 21 (Reuters) - US Secretary of State Marco Rubio said on Wednesday that decisions regarding Ukraine’s access to Starlink were up to SpaceX and Elon Musk, not the White House, comments that suggested Musk may have restricted Kyiv’s access to the service.
The Wall Street Journal reported on Tuesday that Musk had ordered the slowdown of a military-grade version of Starlink that Ukraine relies on to defend itself against missile attacks from Russia.
The Journal cited one source saying that Musk, President Donald Trump and White House officials discussed the matter beforehand, and two sources saying that Musk and the president discussed the matter in the days after the slowdown.
"I’m not aware that we knew about this decision beforehand. But that’s irrelevant," Rubio told reporters during a trip to India.
"The bottom line is that that is governed by a private commercial contract as to how their stuff can be used and what speeds they’ll allow it to be used at." Musk and SpaceX did not respond to Reuters requests for comment.
Reuters has cited two US officials and a Western official briefed on the matter saying the decision ultimately came from the White House. This version was also asserted by Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskiy, but denied by the administration.
Rubio’s comments are likely to intensify concerns in Washington regarding Musk’s singular ability to influence US foreign policy. They also represent an apparent shift in position for the administration.
Trump has publicly said he believed neither he nor Musk was behind the slowdown. Departing for a trip to Uzbekistan and India on Saturday, Rubio had said no one ordered the slowdown, an assertion that drew criticism from lawmakers in both parties.
"I’m not sure Zelenskyy knows what he’s talking about, but it wasn’t deliberate," Rubio said at the time.
"We have nothing to do with that. I don’t – the United States, nobody ordered that Starlink speed to be slowed down. It sort of happened, but my understanding is it’s been restored," Rubio said.
Speaking to reporters on Tuesday, Pentagon chief Pete Hegseth also portrayed the Starlink cutoff as a commercial matter. No US official has publicly said, however, that they have pushed SpaceX to reverse any cutoffs.
"There are terms of service that ultimately need to be complied to, and that’s where Starlink has the option to make those decisions," Hegseth said.
One significant point of confusion relates to the difference between SpaceX’s Starshield and Starlink products. Starshield is essentially a military-grade version of Starlink developed for the Pentagon.
Rubio suggested on Saturday that Ukraine never had access to Starshield in the first place, while Zelenskiy has said that both Starlink and Starshield in Ukraine have been disrupted.

title: This is the single-biggest obstacle to a SpaceX-Tesla merger: JPMorgan
full_text:
Investing.com -- Regulatory approval in China, not Tesla shareholder opposition, is the single biggest obstacle to a SpaceX-Tesla merger, JPMorgan analyst Rajat Gupta warned in a note Wednesday — and the bank is already sketching a TikTok-style structural workaround to get there.
Elon Musk disclosed on SpaceX’s third-quarter 2026 earnings call that special committees have been formed at both Tesla and SpaceX to formally explore a combination.
JPMorgan’s deal math centers on a 30-35% premium to Tesla’s current market cap — a range Gupta describes as typical for transactions of this size and one that would simultaneously imply a merger of equals and secure Musk’s position above the 50% voting-control threshold in the combined company.
Musk reinforced that position in June 2026 by exercising his 2018 award and lifting his TSLA voting stake to approximately 20%, a move JPMorgan views as deliberate preparation for any forthcoming vote.
"The strategic logic for a combination remains coherent," Gupta wrote, "both companies share engineering talent, AI infrastructure, the Terafab chip facility in Texas, and, most importantly, Musk’s leadership and engineering philosophy."
Existing commercial ties deepen the case: SPCX has purchased Tesla Megapack batteries and Cybertrucks, while Tesla invested $2 billion in xAI, now part of SpaceX, according to JPMorgan.
SpaceX’s current valuation stands at approximately $2.0 trillion, up roughly 10% since its IPO, providing what Gupta calls "high-value acquisition currency" for an all-stock bid. JPMorgan analyst Doug Anmuth more than doubled his price target on SPCX to $500.
Yet JPMorgan is candid that the harder problem is Beijing, not Burlingame. China accounts for roughly 20% of Tesla’s revenue and an even higher share of its EBIT and free cash flow.
Gupta acknowledges it is a smaller contributor (around 10%) to the bank’s approximately $1.7 trillion sum-of-the-parts valuation of Tesla, which is skewed toward long-term robotaxi and Optimus value, but the operational reality of Tesla’s large and profitable Shanghai manufacturing footprint makes Chinese regulatory consent unavoidable.
Compounding the difficulty are SpaceX’s deep ties to U.S. defense contracts and the fact that Starlink has never received operating approval in China.
"While Musk has publicly acknowledged the challenges with #1, we believe #2 is likely to prove the bigger hurdle to navigate," Gupta wrote, referring to TSLA shareholder approval as obstacle one and China regulatory clearance as obstacle two.
JPMorgan’s proposed solution borrows from a recent geopolitical precedent.
"We believe one such avenue would be to ring-fence TSLA’s China business or transfer control (a potential mirror image of the US/TikTok arrangement)," Gupta wrote, describing "a potential structure where a China-based consortium controls >50% of the stake, and TSLA continues to generate revenue via a licensing structure for its brand, FSD technology (walled-off) and other future arrangements around Optimus."
The structure would let Beijing retain control of the Chinese entity while Tesla monetizes the business through royalties rather than direct ownership.
Backing the broader deal thesis is what Gupta frames as Musk’s long-term ambition. "Layered atop this is Musk’s well-documented consolidation track record and the end thesis of unifying the AI ecosystem under a single corporate roof."

Investing.com -- PHP released emergency patches today fixing two critical remote code execution vulnerabilities rated CVSS v4.0 9.2, affecting every web server running PHP 5.4 or later — a population spanning an estimated 70% of the world’s websites.
The flaws, collectively dubbed PHP2Shell (CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619), were patched in four simultaneous releases: versions 8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36 and 8.2.35.
Cloudflare Inc (NYSE: NET) is one stock most exposed to this crisis: its Web Application Firewall is the frontline commercial barrier between attackers and millions of PHP sites, and the stock is trading at $307.79, up $16.10 (+5.52%) intraday on Wednesday as investors price in the company’s prominent mitigation role. Other cybersecurity stocks, like CrowdStrike and Palo Alto Networks, are also up.
The trouble started before the patch even shipped. Cloudflare logged the first attacks against PHP sites at 07:43 UTC on October 21, hours before the official patch window opened at approximately 14:00 UTC. Details of the vulnerabilities had leaked publicly on October 20, one day ahead of the coordinated embargo date, forcing the PHP security team to accelerate its release timeline, according to background reporting from sansec.io.
Cloudflare CTO Dane Knecht moved quickly. "PHP sites behind Cloudflare already have an initial set of WAF rules deployed for the known exploit vectors in these vulnerabilities. The rules are available to all customers, including free," he said. Knecht added that the WAF rules are "a STOPGAP only" and urged site operators to apply the official patches as soon as possible, noting the company was updating mitigations as new attack vectors emerged.
The technical stakes are high. CVE-2026-109618 not only enables remote code execution but also carries a Heartbleed-style memory leak capable of exposing passwords, session tokens, API keys and TLS private keys from other server requests — without the application ever calling session_start(), per sansec.io. That combination of code execution and passive credential harvesting makes these vulnerabilities particularly dangerous for shared-hosting environments running WordPress, Drupal, Joomla or Magento.
Governments are already pulling sites offline as a precaution. Reuters reported that cybersecurity agency websites in the Netherlands and Finland went dark, including, ironically, the Dutch National Cyber Security Centre itself. The Dutch House of Representatives and security news site Security.NL also suspended operations. Cybersecurity agencies across Europe, Australia, Japan and Britain urged PHP operators to update immediately or take their sites offline.
The origins of the discovery carry a notable subplot. OpenAI said its GPT-5.6 Sol model independently found CVE-2026-109618 through its "Patch the Planet" initiative in August 2026, while Wiz Research independently discovered and reported both flaws. OpenAI framed the AI-first discovery as a "Defender’s Window", a coordinated interval in which fixes can be deployed before criminal actors weaponize the same finding.
One critical gap remains: PHP versions 8.1 and earlier receive no official fix. The PHP security team released minimal source backports for PHP 7.4, 8.0 and 8.1 for those building from source, but end-of-life installations running on commercial hosting stacks are permanently exposed unless operators take independent action. "So many embedded installations out there that will never be patched. Too many forgotten, unmaintained apps. There will be a long tail for this one," computer forensics expert Hal Pomeranz said, as quoted by helpnetsecurity.com. Security researcher Kevin Beaumont was equally blunt: "The PHP situation will lead to a mass of incidents, it’s one of the biggest vulns in years."
Two near-term catalysts will determine how this story develops. First, a formal listing on the CISA Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog would trigger mandatory patching deadlines for U.S. federal agencies and would likely accelerate enterprise adoption of WAF services, a direct revenue tailwind for Cloudflare. Second, major managed-hosting providers including WP Engine, Kinsta and SiteGround have not yet confirmed rollout timelines for the updated PHP packages; any delay in pushing patches to shared-hosting customers extends the window of exposure and keeps demand for WAF-layer protection elevated. If new exploit variants surface that bypass the initial WAF rules Cloudflare has deployed, a follow-on PHP patch release could arrive before the end of the week, potentially triggering a second wave of emergency upgrades across the internet’s server base.

full_text:

By Raphael Satter, Rajveer Pardesi and Leo Marchandon
Oct 21 (Reuters) - Government websites in Europe and elsewhere went offline on Wednesday after the disclosure of critical vulnerabilities in a widely used programming language sent website operators scrambling to protect their systems.
Developers of the PHP programming language said Tuesday they had identified two critical vulnerabilities and urged users to update their sites as soon as a fix was released. They said around 1345 GMT on Wednesday that a new version fixing the vulnerabilities was live.
But with reports that hackers were exploiting the flaws to break into websites, government agencies in the Netherlands and Finland were among those that took sites offline ahead of the fix as a precaution.
PHP underpins large parts of the internet, raising concerns that a significant number of websites could be vulnerable to attack.
"PHP is everywhere. It quietly powers WordPress, Drupal, Joomla, and Magento sites, shared hosting platforms, control panels, and an awful lot of software that doesn’t even advertise that it runs PHP under the hood," cybersecurity company Huntress said in a blog post.
Dane Knecht, the chief technology officer of Web and cloud security firm Cloudflare, said that attacks were emerging and Cloudflare was updating its firewall rules as a stopgap measure.
"We are seeing early attacks emerging and are updating mitigations as new vectors show up. This is a STOPGAP only. Patch as soon as PHP releases the update," he said on X.
Wordfence, a security plugin that protects WordPress websites, said all WordPress sites run on a PHP-installed server. It warned that automatic updates would not apply the fix and advised site owners to find out who is responsible for updating PHP on their sites.
Cybersecurity agencies in Europe, Australia, Japan and Britain have urged PHP users to update immediately or take websites offline until patches can be applied. The Dutch cybersecurity agency itself went offline, saying it had done so as a precaution because of the vulnerabilities.
Officials have said that all PHP versions from PHP 5 onward could be affected, although PHP has not yet disclosed which versions are vulnerable.
CRITICAL SOFTWARE
PHP is a programming language used to run websites. When a visitor loads a page, a server running PHP assembles the content and sends it to the browser. It is free, open-source software maintained by volunteers.
It is also among the most widely used software on the internet. PHP runs roughly 75% of websites whose programming language can be identified, according to web technology tracker W3Techs. It is the engine behind WordPress, which powers about 43% of all websites from blogs and small business pages to government portals, online stores and news sites.
Automattic, the company behind WordPress.com, said: "We don’t comment on the details of security issues, but our team is prepared and has been working with the PHP security team to ensure a smooth update."
Security experts said the vulnerabilities could potentially open the door to millions of servers because so many websites rely on the same underlying software. Rather than target victims individually, attackers could scan the internet for systems running vulnerable versions of PHP.
AI-assisted hacking campaigns, which have proliferated in recent weeks, could magnify the threat, said Lukasz Olejnik, a visiting senior research fellow at King’s College London.
"The scale is huge," Olejnik said. "And with AI exploitation may happen instantly, on a large scale."
The risk is particularly acute for small websites run by individuals or organisations with limited technical resources, often on shared hosting services where customers do not directly manage the underlying servers. Security experts said such sites could take longer to patch and remain exposed well after fixes become available.
MASS OUTAGES
In the Netherlands, several organisations followed the example of the National Cyber Security Center and took public-facing websites offline, including the Port of Rotterdam, government portal Overheid.nl, the national soccer association KNVB, the websites the country’s five largest political parties and several hospital websites.
Danish municipal IT company Kombit said it had shut down several services, including the national school communication platform, a spokesperson told Reuters.
Disruption was even more widespread in Finland, where state IT services provider Valtori said government public network services had been taken offline "as a precautionary measure."
France’s Interior Ministry said it had temporarily taken local government administrative websites offline while awaiting a security fix.
The US cybersecurity agency CISA did not respond to emails seeking comment.

A merger would create a single company at the center of Musk’s long-term vision: an integrated technology and manufacturing empire spanning AI, energy, robotics, communications and transportation on Earth and beyond.

title: OpenAI expands Google Cloud access as AI rivals deepen ties
full_text:
Investing.com -- OpenAI is expanding its reach among enterprise developers by bringing its latest artificial intelligence models and Codex coding agent to Google Cloud, giving the ChatGPT maker distribution through all three major U.S. cloud infrastructure providers.
The companies said Wednesday that OpenAI’s models, including GPT-6 Astra, will become available through Google Cloud’s Model Garden and Marketplace in the coming weeks. Developers will also be able to access the models through Google’s Antigravity coding tool.
The arrangement allows businesses to purchase OpenAI’s technology using existing Google Cloud spending commitments. Companies in regulated industries can also use Google’s security controls and data governance tools to deploy OpenAI models and build AI agents.
The deal broadens a relationship that already includes cloud computing. OpenAI began using Google Cloud infrastructure to run ChatGPT and its application programming interface, and the latest agreement adds a distribution channel for selling its models to Google’s customers.
The expansion follows OpenAI’s move to widen access to its technology after its exclusive distribution arrangement with Microsoft ended in April. Amazon Web Services began offering OpenAI models shortly afterward, and Google Cloud now joins the distribution network.
For Google, the agreement adds a prominent competitor’s technology to its cloud platform alongside its own Gemini models. The strategy could help attract businesses that want access to multiple AI providers without committing to a single model ecosystem.
The deal comes as Google Cloud’s growth has accelerated amid strong demand for AI infrastructure. Its annualized revenue growth reached about 82% in the second quarter, up from 63% in the first quarter, according to CNBC. Amazon and Microsoft reported cloud growth of 37% and 42%, respectively.
The broader commercial opportunity is significant for AI developers. Cloud marketplaces give companies an established route to enterprise customers, while allowing buyers to use existing infrastructure budgets and procurement arrangements. Anthropic, a major OpenAI competitor, generated 47% of its 2025 revenue through Amazon and Google cloud platforms, according to its IPO filing reviewed by Reuters.
For OpenAI, wider cloud distribution offers another way to monetize its models beyond consumer subscriptions, as the company seeks to build a larger enterprise business. For Google, hosting OpenAI technology underscores its effort to make its cloud platform attractive to customers regardless of which AI developer they choose.

title: Australia’s Santos trims 2026 output forecast on Alaska oilfield delays
full_text:

Oct 22 (Reuters) - Santos narrowed its 2026 production forecast on Thursday after delays due to bad weather and a pipeline disruption at its Pikka oil project in Alaska, even as third-quarter revenue jumped 78%.
Australia’s second-largest independent oil and gas producer now expects production of 99 million to 102 million barrels of oil equivalent (mmboe) in 2026, compared with its previous projection of 99 to 105 mmboe.
Its sales volume forecast was also narrowed to 102 to 105 mmboe, from 102 to 108 mmboe.
Santos said its full-year outlook took a hit due to delays in commissioning a seawater treatment plant at Pikka, output curtailments following a weather event, and a shutdown of the Kuparuk pipeline after a road accident.
The company said the output at Pikka would be held at around 70,000 barrels per day for a short period before ramping up toward 80,000 barrels per day.
But third-quarter sales revenue rose to $2.01 billion from $1.13 billion a year earlier, matching estimates compiled by Visible Alpha.
Santos’ third-quarter production climbed 23% to a record 26.3 mmboe, boosted by its Barossa LNG project in Australia reaching steady production and the ramp-up of output at Pikka. Sales revenue also benefited from higher realised LNG prices and higher sales volumes from Barossa.
